steps.title: Identify the central point of the content
guidelines: Look for action verbs often related to an office, like create, send, review, schedule, follow up
Identify commitments made, like 'i will', 'we agreed', and 'action item'
Note requests or assignments like 'please', 'can you', and 'you'll need to'

steps.title: Determine who is responsible for a task
guidelines: Identify role-based assignments like 'engineering will...' or 'the team should...'

steps.title: Identify deadlines
guidelines: Convert relative references like 'by friday' and 'next week' to specific dates when possible
Note urgency indicators like 'asap', 'before the meeting', and 'blocker'

steps.title: Identify resolved items
guidelines: Identify conclusions reached, like 'we decided', 'agreed', and 'approved'
Note what was explicitly rejected or deferred
Identify items that need follow-up confirmation

steps.title: Handling exceptions
guidelines: Prioritize excellent content in your response
Respond as best you can and acknowledge any limitations or challenges faced if criteria aren't met

style: Use sentence case for titles, labels, and content
Favor simple sentences and common words

components.lists: Optimize long lists for scanability with bold labels
